requirement:
TypeScript and TSX report only `Comment` attachments. Both recognize `//`
line comments and `/* … */` block comments, including `/** … */`
documentation comments. Decorators remain part of the parsed source.
rationale:
The tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.sources.typescript.attachments`. The marked test is `tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]`. Obligations and the scenarios that cover them: - **Only `Comment` attachments are reported.** The `test.ts` and `test.tsx` cases assert the exact list of (kind, text) pairs for every attachment found in the outline, and every expected entry is `Comment`. The source in each case also contains `@dec class C {}`. A decorator wrongly reported as an `Annotation` attachment would add an entry and fail the equality assertion. - **`//` line comments are recognized.** Both cases include a trailing `// trailing` and expect it as a `Comment`. - **`/* … */` block comments, including `/** … */`, are recognized.** The `.ts` case expects `/** doc */` and the `.tsx` case expects `/* doc */`. - **Comment-like text in strings and JSX is not reported.** The `.ts` string `'// string'` and the `.tsx` JSX text `

// text

` are absent from the expected output. Treating these as comments would fail the assertions. - **Decorators remain part of the parsed source.** For `test.ts` and `test.tsx`, the test asserts `snapshot.text().contains("@dec class C")`. Minor asymmetry: the `.ts` case covers only the doc form and the `.tsx` case covers only the ordinary block form. I checked the implementation only to see whether the two languages classify comments differently. In `src/outline/languages/typescript.rs`, the `TYPESCRIPT` profile sets `is_comment: kind_is_comment`, `attaches: never` and `hashes_comment: never`. Comment handling is therefore shared and decorators are never attachments. The asymmetry is not a requirement gap. No gaps were found, and there are no acknowledgments.
